Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with complaints of right shoulder pain and restricted
range of motion. The mechanism of injury described is consistent with the reported symptoms, and the presentation is plausible
for a collision of this type. Examination demonstrated tenderness over the anterior shoulder, reduced active abduction, and pain
with resisted rotation. Imaging findings clearly confirm the soft tissue injury identified on examination. The patient's history
includes a minor strain to the same shoulder several years ago, which resolved completely without residual limitation and did not
require ongoing care. Treatment over three visits consisted of supervised range-of-motion exercises, activity modification, and
as-needed anti-inflammatory medication. Care followed a typical course, with progressive improvement in strength and pain
scores, and visit frequency tapered as the patient recovered. Billing records reflect single, non-duplicated charges for each
encounter. At the final visit the patient reported near-resolution of symptoms and was discharged to a home exercise program
with instructions to return if symptoms recur.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
